Medical History

- Current health concerns and risk factors:
  - Acute upper lip swelling after consuming prawn soup (~7:00 PM); onset ~30 minutes post-ingestion; progressive enlargement.
  - Difficulty breathing; possible chest tightness; dizziness during call.
  - Known peanut allergy since childhood; history of severe reaction at ~age 6 requiring hospital care and an injection (details unknown).
  - Asthma; uses salbutamol inhaler; no preventer (“brown”) inhaler reported.
  - Prior episode ~1 year ago after late-night Chinese meal with heavy alcohol intake; woke with swelling and difficulty breathing; no specific treatment recalled other than using salbutamol.
  - Clinician suspected anaphylactic reaction during this consult.

  - Not recorded.

  - Salbutamol inhaler for asthma (dose/route/frequency not documented).
  - Antihistamines used intermittently for peanut allergy (agent/dose/route/frequency not documented); initially none on hand, later mother confirmed availability at home (timing/context change noted).
  - Denies use of a preventer (“brown”) inhaler.

Management Plan

- Immediate actions:
  - Clinician advised calling an ambulance due to suspected anaphylaxis.
  - Patient instructed to remain with someone; mother to call emergency services (999) and report suspected anaphylactic reaction.
  - Patient advised to take available antihistamine while awaiting ambulance arrival.
- Follow-up:
  - Clinician requested post-hospital follow-up to arrange further allergy management, including injections (epinephrine auto-injector implied) and ongoing plan.

- Internal contradictions:

- Transcript quality:
